recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片下方有一群聚集成片的上皮樣組織球（epithelioid histiocytes），核呈卵圓至拉長形、染色質細緻，細胞質豐富淡藍且邊界不清，混在正常造血細胞中，代表肉芽腫碎片，符合類肉瘤病（sarcoidosis）。
features: Aggregate of epithelioid histiocytes at the bottom of the field
Oval to elongated, slipper-shaped nuclei with fine, pale chromatin and small nucleoli
Abundant pale blue cytoplasm with indistinct cell borders forming a syncytial sheet
Background of normal trilineage hematopoiesis including neutrophils, erythroid precursors and lymphocytes
No organisms or necrotic debris identified
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows an aggregate of epithelioid histiocytes with oval to elongated nuclei, fine chromatin and abundant pale blue syncytial cytoplasm, representing a granuloma fragment. The surrounding marrow contains maturing granulocytes, erythroid precursors and lymphocytes without an atypical population. No necrosis or microorganisms are identified in this field. Findings are consistent with granulomatous marrow involvement, compatible with sarcoidosis after exclusion of infection.

ddx.vs: Infectious granulomas more often show caseous necrosis and organisms on AFB/GMS stains and culture; sarcoidosis is a diagnosis of exclusion.

Carcinoma cells have round pleomorphic nuclei with prominent nucleoli and cohesive cell borders and are cytokeratin-positive, whereas epithelioid histiocytes have bland elongated nuclei and are CD68-positive.
Lymphoma-associated granulomas are accompanied by Reed-Sternberg cells or atypical lymphocytes on biopsy and immunostains.
Morphology is similar; medication history (e.g., checkpoint inhibitors) is the discriminator.
